function: Channel estimation: CNN jointly learns pilot-phase hybrid beamformers and an initial AoA/AoD/delay estimator; gradient-based refinement then reconstructs the beam-squint channel (p. 2, 5-9).
system: MIMO-OFDM TDD, hybrid beamforming: BS NR=32 antennas, 4 RF chains; user NT=16 antennas, 1 RF chain; M=8 subcarriers; fc=28 GHz, B=3 GHz; no RIS (p. 10).
method: CNN (one convolutional and two fully connected layers) trained supervised on channel-to-geometric-parameter pairs with constrained early weights as beamformers; non-learned gradient refinement follows (p. 6-10).
data_channel: Simulated Saleh-Valenzuela channel with beam squint, L=3 paths with site-specific restricted AoA/AoD/delay ranges, path gains CN(0,1); 10^5 training samples, SNR -15 to 15 dB (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Train and test channel ranges identical; trained on mixed SNR (-15 to 15 dB), tested over SNR; retrained for each beam configuration and path count (p. 10-13).
baselines: LS, SOMP, SIGW, GSOMP, GSEM, BSA-SBL (classical); Data-Driven DL [30] (learned); OLS oracle lower bound; isotropic beamformers for the classical methods (p. 10).
metrics: NMSE of channel estimation (primary); RMSE of AoA, AoD and delay; effective SNR of the beamformers; accuracy of path-count estimate (p. 10-13).
complexity: Online CNN: conv layers O(sum Nkernel Nimg Nslice Nslice') and FC layers O(sum Nneuron Nneuron' + 3 Lmax Nneuron); refinement O(3TL(L+1)B^2M^2); training excluded (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 4: "the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model accounting for the beam squint effect is employed" is a custom simulated channel; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "channel parameter ranges in all training sets are identical to" those of the evaluation; p. 12: "Separate training is carried out for each beam" configuration; p. 13: "we retrain and resimulate" for varying L. The SNR sweep and retraining per condition do not count; no unseen scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 10: "LS: The conventional method overlooking sparsity property" and "SOMP and SIGW: The methods that do not consider" beam squint (non-learned), and "Data-Driven DL: The data-driven method that directly" outputs the channel [30] (earlier learned); p. 12: "considerably exceeds comparison methods" on NMSE (Fig. 7).
q4_support: p. 9: "The computational complexity of the proposed method is" analyzed for the CNN layers and the refinement; p. 10: "the computation demanded for the overall" refinement is O(3TL(L+1)B^2M^2).
q5_support: p. 10: "training samples are utilized" (10^5 samples from the authors' own simulation, "A channel estimation simulation is implemented"); no code or data link or public dataset is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included, area 2: the CNN yields the pilot-phase hybrid beamformers and the initial AoA/AoD/delay estimate, refined by a non-learned gradient method, and the main metric is channel NMSE (p. 11: "which is the primary focus of" the paper). Channel is a custom Saleh-Valenzuela simulator (q1=0); training and test distributions are identical and each configuration is retrained (q2=0).
